newsitem.title: USA: Texaco, Chevron earnings squeezed by higher oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Texaco, Chevron earnings squeezed by higher oil prices.

text.p: Texaco Inc. and Chevron Corp. reported higher earnings Thursday, although a jump in crude oil and natural gas prices put a damper on refining profit margins during the fourth quarter.
Texaco said its net income rose to $380 million, or $1.41 a share, in the fourth quarter, compared with year-earlier profits of $367 million, or $1.35 a share.
The White Plains, N.Y.-based company said its revenues rose to $12.87 billion from $9.64 billion.
Texaco said its profit margins, especially on the West Coast, were squeezed by higher crude prices.
For 1996, the company reported earnings of $2.01 billion, or $7.52 a share vs. 1995 profits of $607 million or $2.10 a share. Revenues jumped to $45.50 billion from $36.78 billion.

Chevron said it earned $464 million or 71 cents a share in the fourth quarter compared with a loss of $418 million of 64 cents a share, which stemmed from a charge of $869 million for adopting a new accounting standard. Excluding the charge, year-ago earnings were $241 million, it said.

The San Francisco-based company said its revenues for the quarter soared 25 percent to $11.5 billion from $9.2 billion, with the gain spurred by higher crude oil, natural gas and refined products prices.

"Although the higher oil and gas prices boosted upstream (exploration and production) earnings, they reduced downstream (refining and marketing) and chemicals results because market competition prevented the higher raw material and fuel costs from being recovered in the marketplace," the company said.
"Consequently, sales margins for refined products, such as gasoline, and chemicals were severely squeezed," it said.

For 1996, Chevron said it had record earnings of $2.6 billion, or $3.99 a share, up from 1995's profit of $930 million or $1.43 a share, when a change of accounting standard and other special charges reduced its earnings by $1.032 billion. Revenues rose to $42.78 billion from $36.31 billion.

Occidental Petroleum Corp. said it earned $159 million, or 41 cents a share, on sales of $2.8 billion in the fourth quarter, compared with a loss of $7 million, or 5 cents a share, on sales of $2.5 billion a year earlier.
The 1995 fourth-quarter results included a $132 million charge to reorganize its crude oil and gas and natural gas transmission divisions.
The Los Angeles-based company said earnings from its oil and gas business more than doubled, while natural gas transmission earnings rose about 27 percent. Chemical earnings fell by about a third.
For all of 1996, Occidental said it earned $668 million or $1.77 a share on revenues of $10.55 billion compared with 1995 earnings of $511 million or $1.31 a share on revenues of $10.42 billion.
Texaco's stock rose $1.875 to $108.875, Chevron was up 25 cents at $67.375, and Occidental Petroleum was up 12/5 cents at $26.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
